# Model formats

The glTF container, accessor and mesh transform readers adapt the corresponding C# code from [Humanoid Retargeter](https://github.com/zeljkovranjes/humanoid-retargeter): `GltfDocument.cs` and `GltfModelDmxWriter.cs`. They produce the rigger's canonical character data and use the existing anatomical solver.

Import/export conventions follow the [glTF 2.0 specification](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/glTF/tree/main/specification/2.0): metres, Y up, inverse bind matrices, sparse accessors and packed metallic/roughness textures. Native material preparation retains the retargeter's texture matching and material compilation code.

The archived [specular/glossiness extension](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/glTF/tree/main/extensions/2.0/Archived/KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness) is also supported. Its original factors and maps are retained for direct glTF export. Native preview and prepared exports convert them to metallic/roughness, decoding image RGB to linear light and keeping diffuse opacity separate from glossiness. The conversion is an approximation where the two material workflows differ. The equations were checked against Microsoft's [glTF SDK PBR utilities](https://github.com/microsoft/glTF-SDK/blob/master/GLTFSDK/Inc/GLTFSDK/PBRUtils.h); no SDK dependency is shipped. Extension-selected WebP images are decoded locally and converted to PNG for portable glTF exports.

[Emissive strength](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/glTF/tree/main/extensions/2.0/Khronos/KHR_materials_emissive_strength) preserves HDR emission, including constant colors without an emissive texture. Normal-map scale and occlusion strength are retained in direct glTF exports and baked into separate texture copies for native materials and prepared exports. Occlusion reads the linear red channel, including shared metallic/roughness/occlusion maps. FBX emission properties and OBJ/MTL `Ke` colors also retain emission on export and reimport.

The OBJ reader, polygon triangulation and glTF/OBJ exporters are implemented in C#. No external conversion executable or runtime package is required. The [Khronos glTF Validator](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/glTF-Validator) is used only for local development verification and is not shipped.
